name: Roger Federer
rankNote: retired legend; on the roster as Ryan's pick (Nov 9 2026), not in the live top 20
era: peak headband era, about 2004–2012 (white headband, short tousled dark hair). Earlier look, 2001: short ponytail with a headband or bandana and a bead necklace, worn when he beat Sampras at Wimbledon
signature: the white headband over short, tousled dark hair, plus a smooth, upright one-handed backhand; looks calm and almost effortless
exaggerate: bright white headband, a little thicker than real, with hair flopping over it
long, flowing one-handed backhand follow-through with the free arm stretched back
upright, relaxed posture; light, gliding footwork (no grunting, few big gestures)
source: personality and looks: public media, one link per claim in `sources` (Nov 9 2026); build and height (about 1.85 m) are general knowledge and still need to be checked; outfits wait on stills (#18) Body numbers added Nov 11 2026 from the 2026 ATP media guide where the player is listed, otherwise the source named in body.

grass.notes: all-white dress code. Walk-on: a cardigan (2008) and an all-white military-style jacket with gold details (2009), a possible walk-on animation. Trim colours to research

hard.notes: Headband era. No US Open shirt colour was sourced, so the shirt stays white rather than a guessed polo. The white headband is the signature.

clay.notes: Clay shirt colour withheld for the same reason. White headband stays.

personality.temperament: calm and composed at his peak, rarely angry or pumped up; as a teenager he was hot-headed and smashed rackets, then taught himself to stay calm
personality.style: elegant attacker built around a one-handed backhand
celebrations: tears on court after the biggest wins
personality.notes: public media for temperament, the calm-after-2001 change, tears and his backhand; mannerisms need clips
toConfirm: flicks hair away and adjusts the headband between points
quiet fist pump rather than a big roar
all-court game, comes in to volley

sources.claim: hot-headed as a teenager; smashed a racket in 2001, then worked on staying calm
'the hothead discovers his zen': went from tantrums to composure
stays calm on purpose ('you have to really force yourself')
hair over the headband; does not grunt or wail
hairstyle timeline: ponytail and bandana in 2001, then the headband
2001 Wimbledon v Sampras: white headband, short ponytail, bead necklace
the one-handed backhand as the most beautiful part of his game
Wimbledon walk-on: cardigan (2008), white military-style jacket with gold details (2009)
tears on court after big wins
Wikipedia infobox: 1.85 m, right-handed, one-handed backhand
Tennis Companion ATP-derived table: 1.85 m / 85 kg

body.weightNote: Wikipedia's infobox (read Nov 11 2026) gives height and the one-handed backhand, not weight. 85 kg is the figure on Tennis Companion's ATP-derived table and on the same comparison pages that list Nadal at 85 kg. Marked from that secondary table, not from the 2026 media guide (the legends page omits height and weight).

reachM.note: Same formula as bodyStats() in index.html. Not a measured wingspan. datasets/players/<id>/body.json does not exist yet (Body Scout has not run).

letRate.note: Same range already used for Sinner (0.02) and Alcaraz (0.03): lets on roughly 1–3% of pro serves. Not counted from a match log.

skills.scale: 1–20, 10 = neutral, the Skills Coach scale in src/skills/skills.js
skills.note: Not a measured rating. Set from the published style already in this file (serve size, footspeed, touch) so the locker room is not all 10s.

torsoScale.note: look.torso in src/players/roster.js is a pixel width multiplier taken from words already in signature/exaggerate (lanky, broad, slim). It is not a measured shoulder width.

favouriteServes.summary: Varied serve from one toss; slice and kick both part of the one-handed game.
